lc_person: Randy Sanders, historian at Southeastern Louisiana University; author of Mighty Peculiar Elections (2002; reprinted 2007).
item_person: Morton Masius (1883–1979), chemist and physicist at Worcester Polytechnic Institute.

evidence.says: The authorized heading is Sanders, Randy. Its source is Mighty peculiar elections (2002), whose book information identifies Randy Sanders as an assistant professor of history at Southeastern Louisiana University.

Q1690837 is labeled Morton Masius and describes a chemist and physicist (1883–1979); its employer is Worcester Polytechnic Institute. It nevertheless carries P244 n2002105508, VIAF 46821521 and ISNI 0000000014043424.

Mighty Peculiar Elections is assigned to the supplied author OL2839347A. Editions include University Press of Florida, 2002 (ISBN 9780813025650; LCCN 2002027135), and Louisiana State University Press, 2007 (ISBN 9780807132906; LCCN 2007028972). This matches the work cited by LC.

The publisher credits Randy Sanders with Mighty Peculiar Elections: The New South Gubernatorial Campaigns of 1970 and the Changing Politics of Race, published in 2007, and identifies him as a history professor.
The publisher identifies Randy Sanders as a historian who taught at Southeastern Louisiana University for twenty years and wrote Mighty Peculiar Elections.

The enriched LC data links the Sanders authority to Q1690837, VIAF 46821521 and ISNI 0000000014043424 despite retaining the Sanders heading and historical book citation. These cross-links conflict with the authority’s own identifying source.

notes: The P244 association is a mismatch, also reflected in LC external cross-links. The supplied Open Library author includes the matching historical book alongside other titles; the exact book match supports lc_fits_key. No verified Wikidata item for the historian was found. LC supplies no birth year; 1883 belongs to Masius and should not be assigned to Sanders.
